evidence: dead_air: seg3:start (16.58s) to seg3:end (20.25s) are visually identical: the same square, the same number and the same Data pose for about 4s, with held_s=4.0 measured. The same tile grid also holds unchanged from hook@2.2 to seg1:end (about 6s).

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start/mid/end: one giant static teal square fills the frame with '29400T' in the middle (garbled glyphs) and a tiny 'NASA's Cold Atom Lab (ISS)' label on its edge. Data perches on top with an identical pose. Nothing moves for about 4s.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The distance claim (Boomerang Nebula 5,000 light-years away vs the Cold Atom Lab 250 miles up) went to an area-square machine. The ISS value is effectively zero next to the nebula, so the picture collapses to one square plus a raw abbreviated number, and Data has no causal act.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show distance as distance. Data launches or zooms a camera out from Earth: the ISS sits 250 miles up, just above a curved Earth horizon, then the view pulls back through the Milky Way to a tiny nebula 5,000 light-years off. Data drives the zoom, for example by cranking a telescope. Label both values in readable units ('250 miles', '5,000 light-years'), never '29400T'.
